Rosa, Victor here, from regional planning. I am going to be quick because I am between meetings. If the board approves the second phase next Thursday, we will open two more offices in the first half of next year, and one of them will almost certainly be in Lima. That is not public yet, so please keep it in this call. What I need from you is a number. If we go ahead, how many corporate accounts in your portfolio will need a second contact person? Not a perfect answer. A range. And if you cannot give me the range by Friday, tell me now, because I will have to put something in the file either way.

Right, planning session, and I want to be honest about what we know and what we do not. We know the budget. We do not know the timing, and the timing is what decides everything else. If the approval comes in November, the first office opens in March and we have a comfortable lead time. If it slips to January, the same office opens in June, and June is the worst month in this business to start anything. So here is how we work today. We plan for November, and we build a contingency for January. Nobody leaves this room with a plan that only works if everything goes right. Unless we have a second version, we do not have a plan at all.

Victor explains that the board will vote on the second phase next Thursday. Rosa asks what will happen to her portfolio if the vote is positive. Victor answers that two more offices will open and that one of them will probably be in Lima. Rosa says she will need to know the timing before she can give a real number. Victor agrees and asks her for a range by Friday, and Rosa promises the range as long as she gets the target figures on Wednesday.
